issues.description: Attribute type mismatch: the problem statement's UML defines numberOfInscribedStudents as int, but the solution implementation declares numberOfInscribedStudents as long. This creates a structural inconsistency in the expected attribute types, affects the constructor signature, getters/setters, and can confuse students about which type to use.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent. Either change numberOfInscribedStudents in the solution to int to match the UML/problem statement, or update the UML/problem statement and all method signatures to use long (including constructor parameter and getter/setter return/param types). Prefer changing the solution attribute to int to match the UML and problem description.

issues.description: Method return/type incompatibility: getTotalNumberOfStudents() is specified in the UML/problem as returning int, and the solution declares it as int, but its implementation adds a long attribute (numberOfInscribedStudents) to an int (numberOfGuestStudents). Summing long and int yields a long, so returning an int from that expression is a type mismatch and will not compile. This inconsistency between attribute type and method return type creates a structural error students will encounter.
issues.suggestedFix: Ensure return types and operand types are compatible. Either change getTotalNumberOfStudents() to return long (and update UML/problem if intended), or change numberOfInscribedStudents to int so the sum is an int. Keep the UML, template, and solution consistent (recommended: change the solution attribute to int, or else update the UML to indicate a long and change the method return type to long).
